description: A Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model for predicting the probability of a Fenwick (unblocked) shot attempt converting into a goal.  Contextual features such as the number of seconds from the last event and whether the shot occured on the opposite side of the ice from the last event are included alongside shot location. Due to recent changes in NHL tracking data, including the addition of special shot types such as "short" and "behind-net" and the automation of shot locations, the latest xG model is trained on data from the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons only.

Implementation of RAPM models expanded by a player's observed time on ice for their "total" value, using an adjustment from the league-average to express the value of a player's individual contributions in terms of goals, above a replacement level NHL (which are somewhat below average skaters or goaltenders).
A general linear model primarily designed to describe single-game performances by skater in NHL games.  Model is trained on regular season games from 2023-24 to 2024-25.

A simulation engine utilizing both individual performance estimates (from the RAPM models) and observed rates in conjunction with league-based constants to simulate the outcomes of NHL games.  This engine is primarily utilized to predict the likeliest sets of outcomes for NHL games, including the victor, team outputs, and individual player box-score statistics.
